criteria.text: The response identifies that 'Fundamental Representations' are defined by cross-reference to Disclosure Schedule Section 1.1(f), and that this schedule section omits SPA Section 4.14 (Environmental Matters). It concludes that environmental breaches therefore fall under the 10% cap in SPA Section 9.4(a), contrary to the Drapesk board consent's approval of Section 4.14 as a Fundamental Representation. The response locates the issue in the Disclosure Schedule Section 1.1(f) and/or SPA Sections 1.1 and 9.4(a). It explains why this matters to Drapesk and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the 6-month survival period in SPA Section 9.1 can expire before Buyer is able to bring an environmental (Section 4.14) claim. The reason it gives is that Section 9.6 bars such claims until 30 days after the Phase II Report, and Section 6.8 allows that report to arrive up to 180 days after Closing. The response locates the issue in SPA Sections 9.1 and 9.6 (with 6.8). It explains why this matters to Drapesk and recommends a fix.
hints: six months after the Closing Date
30 days after receipt of the Phase II Report

criteria.text: The response identifies that SPA Section 11.5 lets Seller assign the Agreement or its rights or obligations to any Person without Buyer's consent, and releases Seller from its obligations on assignment. It notes that the assignable obligations include Seller's indemnity and/or its covenants. The response locates the issue in SPA Section 11.5. It explains why this matters to Drapesk and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that SPA Section 9.3(b) has Buyer indemnify Seller for Losses from Company operations 'whether before or after the Closing'. It identifies that SPA Section 9.4(c) excludes Section 9.3(b) from Buyer's cap. It concludes that Buyer bears uncapped liability for pre-Closing Company liabilities. The response locates the issue in SPA Sections 9.3(b) and 9.4(c). It explains why this matters to Drapesk and recommends a fix.
hints: whether before or after the Closing

criteria.text: The response states that the Purchase Price is $184,000,000.
The response states that Seller's general indemnity cap under SPA Section 9.4(a) is 10% of the Purchase Price.
The response states that the Indemnity Escrow Amount is $9,200,000.
The response is written as a memo with a separate entry for each issue. Each entry states the document and section, why the issue matters to Drapesk, and a recommended fix.

The response claims that, under the SPA as currently drafted, Section 4.14 (Environmental Matters) is a Fundamental Representation exempt from the 10% cap, including by operation of the Section 11.9 order-of-precedence clause.
The response claims that the 6-month survival period gives Buyer sufficient time to bring a claim for breach of Section 4.14 after receiving the Phase II Report.
